newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Most Kuwaiti debtors adhere to payment deadline.
newsitem.headline: Most Kuwaiti debtors adhere to payment deadline.

text.p: Most Kuwaiti debtors obliged to meet a Sept. 6 repayment deadline under a plan to settle billions of dollars in bad debt met the deadline and repaid millions of dollars, bankers said on Sunday.
"Turnout was very good. We've had almost 95 percent of the debtors making payments or registering for a delayed payment," a banker said.
Debtors have the option to delay payment for six months, but they then incur a penalty of 15 percent interest.
"Generally it seems that about 75 percent amounts due were paid," said a banker.
The exact amounts repaid are usually announced by the central bank a few days after the deadline.
Banks managing a programme to end the Gulf state's thorniest economic problem received payments from about 80 percent of the hundreds of debtors who were due to meet the deadline, bankers said.
The banks will send names of debtors who did not meet the deadline to the state prosecutor for possible bankruptcy proceedings.

The payments were meant to settle the second of five annual instalments due under a so-called cash settlement option of a plan to recover billions of dollars in non-performing loans that have blighted the economy for 14 years.
The debt stems in part from the 1982 crash of an unofficial stock market played by wealthy Kuwaitis using bank loans and from commercial losses caused by Iraq's 1990-91 occupation.

The debt is owed by about 10,000 borrowers, including senior government officials and merchants, whose original obligations of about $20 billion were equivalent to 90 percent of the national wealth as measured by gross domestic product.

Under the plan those who do not pay could face bankruptcy proceedings. Officials have said these may include a ban on overseas travel by debtors or their close relatives, a ban on debtors' participation in parliamentary elections as candidates or voters and a ban on their participation in commerce.
